what: User decision (2026-10-20): girihelix ports Java's list sort into PlanarMap.Order.sort/3 so edge and vertex order match Taprats exactly under the non-transitive 1e-7 comparators. That means binary insertion below 32 elements (after the initial run detection, with a strictly descending run reversed) and TimSort above. It must reproduce Java's sequence of comparisons, because with a non-transitive comparator a different sort algorithm gives a different order. Write it from the published algorithm description, never from OpenJDK source: OpenJDK is GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception, which is incompatible with girihelix's GPLv3. Its correctness is judged by fuzz golden scenarios against real Taprats.
why: The final review of Plan 1b found Elixir's stable sort diverged from Taprats in 10 of 12 fuzz cases; the user chose faithful reproduction.
